title: E2E latency profiling traces (p50/p95/p99) - 2026-03-05
content:
Summary:

This doc contains end-to-end latency profiling traces captured for the serving runtime during the 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-05 runs. Focus is on p50/p95/p99 latency and per-stage breakdowns to isolate hotspots (routing, enqueue, KV cache, model forward/decoding, post-processing, network). Data comes from distributed trace spans (ingress -> auth -> routing -> enqueue -> kv-cache -> model-exec -> decode -> postproc -> egress) collected across 8 pods in us-west-2 under a steady-state workload.

Objectives:
- Report p50/p95/p99 for representative workloads (small prompt, long prompt, streaming).
- Provide per-stage median and tail timings.
- Surface common trace archetypes and outliers.
- Recommend mitigations (batching, cache tuning, kernel selection).

Methodology:
- Traces sampled at 5% of requests to limit overhead.
- Two test workloads: SMALL (<=64 input tokens, 16 token generation), LARGE (512 input tokens, 128 token generation).
- Both warm and cold-model samples included; warm runs filtered for main table unless noted.
- Times reported in milliseconds. p50/p95/p99 computed on end-to-end wall-clock from ingress receive to final egress.

Aggregate E2E Latency (wall-clock):
- SMALL (warm, non-streaming): p50=42 ms, p95=118 ms, p99=262 ms
- SMALL (cold model load included): p50=120 ms, p95=420 ms, p99=1100 ms
- LARGE (warm, non-streaming): p50=420 ms, p95=980 ms, p99=2300 ms
- LARGE (streaming, chunked): p50=360 ms (first-chunk), p95=850 ms, p99=2100 ms

Per-stage breakdown (median p50 / p95) - SMALL (warm):
- API ingress (parsing + auth): 2 ms / 8 ms
- Smart routing + policy check: 3 ms / 18 ms
- Request enqueue / scheduler wait: 5 ms / 40 ms
- KV cache lookup: 1 ms (hit) / 10 ms (miss)  -- cache hit rate ~72% for this workload
- Model forward (context + init): 20 ms / 70 ms
- Decode (generate 16 tokens): 8 ms / 18 ms
- Post-processing (detokenize, safety hooks): 1 ms / 5 ms
- Network egress: 2 ms / 5 ms
- Total: 42 ms / 118 ms

Per-stage breakdown (median p50 / p95) - LARGE (warm):
- API ingress: 3 ms / 12 ms
- Routing: 4 ms / 26 ms
- Enqueue: 25 ms / 200 ms (batching variance)
- KV cache lookup: 5 ms / 30 ms (many partial cache misses due to long context)
- Model forward (512-context handling): 240 ms / 640 ms
- Decode (generate 128 tokens): 130 ms / 350 ms
- Postproc: 4 ms / 12 ms
- Network egress: 6 ms / 10 ms
- Total: 420 ms / 980 ms

Trace archetypes observed (examples):
1) Typical fast SMALL request (p50 trace sample):
   Ingress 2ms -> Routing 3ms -> Enqueue 4ms -> KV-hit 1ms -> Model-forward 18ms -> Decode 7ms -> Postproc 1ms -> Egress 2ms = 38-42ms

2) Enqueue-wait spike (observed in p95 tails for LARGE):
   Ingress 3ms -> Routing 5ms -> Enqueue 180ms (queue / batch wait) -> KV 6ms -> Model-forward 300ms -> Decode 220ms -> Postproc 5ms -> Egress 6ms = ~725ms (major contributor: enqueue wait + model-forward)

3) Cold-model load (rare p99 events):
   Ingress 3ms -> Routing 6ms -> Enqueue 10ms -> Model load 820ms -> Model-forward 200ms -> rest 10ms = >1050ms (model init dominates)

Outlier patterns and root-cause signals:
- Enqueue/scheduler delays are a consistent contributor to p95/p99 for large-context workloads. Correlates with short bursts where batch size goals (for throughput) exceeded available GPU slots.
- Partial KV cache misses for long contexts: the KV lookup has higher variance when the context page spans multiple sharded cache segments; causes model-forward work to reprocess more context and increases memory-copy overhead.
- Cold starts (model load) remain high-impact but infrequent. Cold events correlate with autoscaling events and node churn in Dedicated clusters.
- Kernel-selection variance: a subset of p95 traces show ~15-25ms overhead added right before model-forward start, traced to a slow kernel fallback path on certain model shapes (detected on 2/8 pods).

Recommendations (short-term):
- Enqueue improvements: implement soft-deadline preemption to cap per-request wait and signal fallback to lower-cost model variant when queue wait exceeds 150ms.
- Batching policy tweak: reduce max batch delay for large-context interactive routes; prefer smaller batch sizes with parallel GPU occupancy heuristics to reduce p95s.
- KV cache: increase shard affinity and prefetch for long contexts; consider 'sticky' routing to pod with warm KV for recent sessions.
- Cold start mitigation: keep minimal warm replicas per model for Dedicated customers with SLA; pre-warm common model variants during traffic spikes.
- Kernel-fallback investigation: reproduce on affected pods (identified via span tag kernel_id) and add targeted telemetry for kernel selection time. Patch expected to reduce 15-25ms overhead on p95 traces.

Recommendations (medium-term):
- Adaptive routing: route requests by estimated cost (context length + expected gen length) to appropriate capacity tiers (high-memory vs low-latency).
- Dynamic quantization profiles for large-context models to reduce forward time while preserving quality; run A/B on a subset of traffic.
- Trace-based alerting: add SLA-tail alerts derived from trace-span composition (e.g., enqueue_time > 150ms OR model_forward > 600ms triggers investigation).

Next steps / Action items:
- Diego to add enqueue preemption prototype (SERVRT-3478) and run a canary against internal traffic next week.
- Priya to add enhanced kernel-selection telemetry and correlate with p95 traces (SERVRT-3490).
- Liam to own KV prefetch experiment and report hit-rate delta (SERVRT-3492).

Appendix: sample raw traces (abbreviated) - each line is CSV style: trace_id, total_ms, ingress_ms, routing_ms, enqueue_ms, kv_ms, model_forward_ms, decode_ms, post_ms, egress_ms
- t-001,38,2,3,4,1,18,7,1,2
- t-002,745,3,5,180,6,300,220,5,6
- t-003,1125,3,6,10,2,820,270,8,6
- t-004,430,4,6,30,8,240,120,6,6
- t-005,68,2,4,10,1,36,12,1,2

Notes about data quality:
- Sampling at 5% biases tail capture slightly; p99 especially may be under-sampled.
- Times exclude client-side retries; retries can amplify observed enqueue waits.

If you want, I can attach the raw span-level traces (ndjson) filtered for warm runs and a notebook that reproduces the per-stage percentiles. For the next update I'll include kernel_id tagging and per-pod breakdown across the 8 pods to localize the kernel fallback.
